title: CFA Level I — Official Mock Exam 1 (Session 1: Morning Paper)

questions.stem: During a portfolio review, Analyst #1 receives material nonpublic information regarding a pending regulatory action against a corporate issuer. According to the CFA Institute Code and Standards, what is the required compliance protocol?

options.A: Act on the information immediately before market open to protect client capital.
options.B: Refrain from trading or causing others to trade until the information is publicly disclosed.
options.C: Inform high-net-worth clients verbally while withholding written research reports.

questions.explanation: Standard II(A) Material Nonpublic Information strictly mandates that members in possession of material nonpublic information must not trade or cause others to trade until public dissemination occurs.
questions.wrongAnalysis:
- Option A is incorrect because trading on material nonpublic information violates Standard II(A).
- Option C is incorrect because selective verbal disclosure to favored clients violates both Standard II(A) and Standard III(B) Fair Dealing.

questions.stem: An investor deposits USD 10,000 into a savings account offering a nominal annual rate of 5.0% compounded quarterly. What is the total investment value at the end of 5 years (20 quarters)?
questions.explanation: Future Value formula: $FV = PV \times (1 + r/4)^{20} = 10000 \times (1 + 0.0125)^{20} = \text{USD } 12,820.37$.
questions.wrongAnalysis:
- Option A is incorrect because it uses simple uncompounded interest (USD 12,500.00).
- Option C is incorrect because it contains a compounding period frequency error.

questions.stem: The price elasticity of demand for a consumer product is estimated at -1.2 (elastic). If the firm increases its retail selling price by 8%, what is the expected impact on total product revenue?

options.C: Total revenue will remain completely unchanged.

questions.explanation: When demand is price elastic ($|E_d| = 1.2 > 1.0$), the percentage drop in quantity demanded exceeds the percentage price increase, causing total revenue to decrease.
questions.wrongAnalysis:
- Option A is incorrect because price and total revenue move in opposite directions when demand is elastic.
- Option C is incorrect because total revenue remains unchanged only under unit elasticity ($|E_d| = 1.0$).
